## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) with \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), Theorem 5.4 gives two generating families indexed respectively by \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\) and \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\), where \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\); each has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-2, lines 1382-1421]
- [source-backed] The paper conjectures that both families are minimal and reports computer verification only for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2, lines 1495-1502]
- [computed] For the first unreported corner instance \((r,n-r,i,j)=(5,6,2,2)\), one has \((a,b,N)=(3,2,10)\). The specialized families are
  \[
  F_1=(22,32,33,42,43,52,44,53,54,55),
  \quad
  F_2=(22,221,2211,222,22111,2221,22211,2222,22221,22222).
  \]
  [artifact e043e3963e2ca3b2a6e531559996e6fdfaf60f0cfcc274c9b277a5a207cc26fc]
- [computed] The attempted degree-block unit-pivot certificate for this instance fails for both \(F_1\) and \(F_2\), first in degree \(7\); thus this computation neither supports nor refutes minimality. It obstructs only this proposed certificate method. [artifact e043e3963e2ca3b2a6e531559996e6fdfaf60f0cfcc274c9b277a5a207cc26fc]
- [source-backed] The stronger statement \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\) was explicitly only suspected by the authors, who state that a proof eluded them. [source-2, lines 1547-1552]

## Strategy
Use \((5,6,2,2)\), immediately outside the reported range, as a finite test case. Compare the two ten-element families against the exact Pieri relation lattice degree by degree.

## Gaps
The failed pivot test is not an independent verification and is not a counterexample. No Smith-form or independently implemented LR computation was produced.

## Next
Construct an exact Smith-normal-form or unimodular-minor certificate for \((5,6,2,2)\), preferably using an independently written LR implementation.
